scorecard.note: Simplify and make the visual concepts concrete so they are instantly understandable on a phone screen.

storyboard.ears: The biggest owners of corporate America aren't tycoons. They're index funds in your account.
Index funds once held a sliver of the stock market. Now they hold over half of it, and they keep buying.
storyboard.eyes: substance: grey seats turning cyan-blue; cause: Data places a reserved card on seat after seat, claiming the hall row by row
storyboard.evidence: Morningstar / S&P Dow Jones Indices fund-flow research (approximate, compiled) | Passive index funds' share of US stock market assets | https://www.morningstar.com | 2026-10-08

storyboard.ears: BlackRock, Vanguard and State Street together own twenty-two percent of a typical big company, over five times the top active manager.
storyboard.eyes: substance: lit office floors; cause: Data pulls the power lever at the tower's base and the owners' share of its floors lights up
storyboard.evidence: Academic/industry research on BlackRock, Vanguard, State Street combined holdings | Combined 'Big Three' stake vs a typical large active manager, avg S&P 500 company | https://www.sec.gov | 2026-10-08

storyboard.ears: Vanguard alone casts nearly one in ten votes at big company shareholder meetings. One firm, that much say.
storyboard.evidence: Academic/industry research on index-fund proxy voting power | Share of S&P 500 annual-meeting votes cast by each 'Big Three' manager | https://www.sec.gov | 2026-10-08

storyboard.ears: Your index fund has a vote. You don't.
